summary:
Oct 5 radar for the GLP-1 focus. The EASD and Lancet wave is still moving down to consumers, and three named-drug stories have now reached mainstream news while consumer and YouTube coverage is still thin. These are the top opportunities:

1. **Trevogrumab + semaglutide muscle data (COURAGE).** Lean-mass loss was 4.2% vs 7.3% (about 42% relative). This fits our muscle pillar well and few creators have covered it.
2. **Foundayo (orforglipron) ACHIEVE-4 in The Lancet.** It met the heart-safety target against insulin glargine.
3. **Survodutide SYNCHRONIZE-2 in NEJM.** Up to 13.1% vs 3.1% placebo, if people stayed on treatment.

Two safety stories are back in the news and should be handled as calm explainers:
- Wegovy and the rare "eye stroke" (NAION): a local-TV vision-loss case plus a FAERS report-signal study.
- The 2.1-million-pregnancy review: no clearly detectable increase in risk after GLP-1 exposure around conception, which is not the same as "proven safe".

Retatrutide and EloraTZP are now peaking. Only cover them as headline decoders (which number, which population, which estimand, the dropout rate). Kids' GLP-1 prescriptions and over-the-counter "GLP-1 support" supplements are rated caution: kids are outside our audience, and the supplement story only works as a careful myth-bust.

What still needs checking:
- The kids' prescription figures from local news ("0.03% to 9.3%") must be checked against the Pediatrics abstract.
- The petrelintide and Wegovy liver-fat numbers weren't checked here.
- For survodutide, use the NEJM paper's sample size, not the press release's 755.

candidates.topic: Trevogrumab + semaglutide: experimental Regeneron antibody cut lean-mass loss to 4.2% vs 7.3% on semaglutide alone at 52 weeks (~42% relative; Phase 2 COURAGE, company-funded, in press at The Lancet)
candidates.angle: 'Can you keep your muscle on semaglutide (Wegovy)?' Explains the new add-on drug result honestly: it's Phase 2, company-funded and not approved, and it didn't meaningfully boost weight loss. Then covers what you can do today: protein (unless your clinician has told you to limit it), strength training and slower loss. Name the drug and comparator in the title.
candidates.predicted_peak: 1–3 weeks (Lancet publication will trigger second wave)
candidates.why_now: Presented at EASD with a Regeneron press release on Oct 1. Medical Daily, Inc. and Pharmacy Times picked it up Oct 3–4. The Lancet paper is still in press, so a second spike will come when it's published. Muscle loss is a top worry for people on GLP-1s, and very few consumer explainers name trevogrumab yet.

evidence.signal: Phase 2 COURAGE: trevogrumab prevents lean mass loss during GLP-1 weight loss; MRI substudy 70% of muscle loss prevented
4.2% vs 7.3% lean mass reduction at 52 weeks, 75 mg dose; company-funded
Trade coverage of semaglutide combinations in COURAGE

candidates.topic: Foundayo (orforglipron) passes heart-safety test: non-inferior to insulin glargine for MACE-4 (HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.59–1.20) in adults with type 2 diabetes at increased cardiovascular risk (ACHIEVE-4, The Lancet)
candidates.angle: 'Is the GLP-1 pill orforglipron (Foundayo) safe for your heart?' Explains what 'non-inferior' means: it's a safety test against insulin, not proof of heart protection. The all-cause death finding (HR 0.43) was nominal and not adjusted for multiple comparisons. Covers who was studied and common GI side effects.
candidates.why_now: Published in The Lancet on Sep 30 with an EASD presentation. HCPLive, Drug Topics and Medical Xpress ran trade or science coverage, but there's almost no consumer video yet. Orforglipron is a named drug our audience is already searching for, and our orforglipron long-form was our top long-form.

evidence.signal: ACHIEVE-4 phase 3 open-label non-inferiority vs insulin glargine
MACE-4 HR 0.84 (0.59–1.20); MACE-3 HR 0.77; all-cause mortality HR 0.43 nominal
Largest and longest T2D study for Foundayo

candidates.topic: Survodutide (glucagon/GLP-1 dual agonist) in adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes: 8.2%/9.8% vs 3.9% placebo at 76 weeks (everyone randomised), up to 13.1% vs 3.1% if on treatment (SYNCHRONIZE-2, NEJM)
candidates.angle: 'What is survodutide, and how does it compare?' A headline decoder: the two ways of counting, why weight loss is usually lower in type 2 diabetes, and the A1C drop of 0.8–0.9 points vs 0.2. Cross-trial comparisons with tirzepatide must be labelled as indirect. Say it isn't approved as of Oct 2026.
candidates.why_now: Published in NEJM on Oct 1, with Healio, AJMC and HCPLive coverage. Searches like 'new weight loss drug for diabetes' are showing in feeds. There's little consumer YouTube content naming survodutide yet. Note: use the NEJM paper's sample size, not the press release's 755.

evidence.signal: Survodutide Once Weekly in Adults with Obesity and Type 2 Diabetes
'Impressive' weight loss in T2D and obesity
Up to 13.1% weight loss

candidates.topic: Semaglutide (Wegovy) and 'eye stroke' (NAION) back in the news: Austin vision-loss case plus a British Journal of Ophthalmology FAERS analysis reporting a stronger signal for Wegovy than Ozempic
candidates.angle: 'Does Wegovy (semaglutide) raise eye-stroke risk?' A calm decoder: what NAION is, how rare it is, and why FAERS report counts can't measure risk. Compare with the cohort data (about a twofold relative risk in some studies) and say what regulators concluded (MHRA, Feb 2026). End with red-flag symptoms (sudden painless vision loss in one eye means seek urgent care) and 'don't stop without talking to your prescriber'.
candidates.why_now: On Oct 5, KXAN Austin ran a local-TV story about a father who lost vision on Wegovy, WSB radio ran a doctor's warning, and Medical Economics ran a 'Wegovy may pose higher risk' item. This is the fear-driven search spike, where a balanced, sourced explainer can stand out. We first flagged the topic in a previous snapshot.

evidence.signal: Local vision-loss case on Wegovy, Oct 5
Wegovy may have highest eye-stroke signal of semaglutide products (FAERS pharmacovigilance)
Semaglutide and NAION, Feb 2026

candidates.topic: GLP-1 exposure around conception: no clearly detectable increase in miscarriage, birth defects, preterm birth or other outcomes in a meta-analysis of 10 studies (2.1 million pregnancies, 8,325 exposed)
candidates.angle: 'Took semaglutide or tirzepatide before finding out you were pregnant?' Reassuring but exact: inadvertent early exposure wasn't linked to a detectable increase, but that is not proof the drugs are safe in pregnancy. The labels still advise stopping before a planned pregnancy, so talk to your prescriber. Include the limitation that the data are observational.
candidates.why_now: Medical Xpress covered it on Oct 5. The Pharmaceutical Journal and Nursing Times also covered it, and a Diabetologia French nationwide study appeared Sep 29. It also links to our earlier postpartum-prescription trend (JAMA, 24-fold rise). 'Ozempic babies' is a recurring viral search.

evidence.signal: Largest review to date, no detectable increase in pregnancy risks
No clear increase; observational limits stressed
French nationwide study of new glucose-lowering agents in T2D pregnancy

candidates.topic: EloraTZP (eloralintide + tirzepatide) 23.3% vs tirzepatide alone 14.8% in adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes, but 27% side-effect dropout (Phase 2)
candidates.angle: 'Lilly's amylin combo: 23.3%, but at what cost?' A headline decoder that puts weight loss next to tolerability: dropout, nausea, what amylin does differently, and the fact that Phase 3 is only planned. No approval as of Oct 2026.
candidates.why_now: Pharmacy Times, Drug Discovery News and TIKR covered it Oct 2–5, and LinkedIn is circulating the 27% dropout figure. It has appeared in 2 previous snapshots (momentum 90 then 88). The amylin story is building, with a petrelintide paper and a Diabetes Therapy review also out.

evidence.signal: EloraTZP up to 23.3% weight loss in obesity + T2D
Lilly's amylin combo raises the bar

candidates.topic: Retatrutide '25% weight loss' headlines decoded: TRIUMPH-2 (Lancet) in adults with T2D and obesity vs the TRIUMPH-1 knee-pain basket. Which number belongs to which trial and estimand
candidates.angle: 'Did retatrutide really cause 25% weight loss?' Match each viral number (25%, 23.4%, 20.8%) to its trial, population, dose and estimand, with placebo alongside. Unapproved as of Oct 2026, and anything sold online isn't Lilly's trial drug.
candidates.why_now: NDTV ('25%'), MedPage, Cardiac Wire and mamabella.uk ran stories Oct 2–5. Many search queries mention retatrutide and an 'FDA concerns unapproved' angle. Coverage is crowded, so our differentiated decoding is what makes it worth doing. Retatrutide titles performed above median for us.

evidence.signal: TRIUMPH-2 phase 3 publication
'25% weight loss' headline
Retatrutide delivers substantial weight loss in T2D

candidates.topic: GLP-1s and hair loss in men: new genetic study suggests extra risk in men prone to pattern baldness (Washington Post), alongside the BMJ comparison vs SGLT2 inhibitors
candidates.angle: 'Does semaglutide or tirzepatide make men lose hair?' Covers what the genetic signal does and doesn't show, the modest relative risk from BMJ, the absolute picture, the role of rapid weight loss (telogen effluvium, usually reversible) and protein habits, and when to see a doctor.
candidates.why_now: The Washington Post ran the story on Oct 3. Hair loss already appeared in 2 previous snapshots and is a high-volume evergreen side-effect search. The men-specific angle is new.

evidence.signal: Possible connection between GLP-1s and hair loss in men

candidates.topic: Semaglutide's kidney protection, under the microscope: Nature Medicine RCT in type 2 diabetes with CKD. Primary MRI outcomes showed no difference, but secondary measures pointed to lower vascular resistance and stalled fibrosis
candidates.angle: 'How does semaglutide (Ozempic) protect kidneys?' Recap FLOW (24% fewer major kidney events in T2D + CKD), then show what the new biopsy and MRI trial adds. Report honestly that the primary outcomes were not significant and the mechanism clues come from secondary outcomes in a small sample.
candidates.why_now: Published in Nature Medicine on Oct 1 by Tuttle and Bjornstad. A Diabetes Obes Metab population study (GLP-1 added to SGLT2) and an Australian panel paper add more fresh hooks. Kidney benefits are a pillar, packaged with a named drug and named comparator.

evidence.signal: Effects of semaglutide on kidney disease in T2D: randomized placebo-controlled trial
FLOW: 24% lower risk of major kidney disease events
Adding GLP-1RA to SGLT2i in CKD, population study

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) linked to lower diabetic retinopathy risk vs lifestyle-only care (Ophthalmology, ~174,000 US patients; mild retinopathy 0.49% vs 1.2%), the counterweight to the eye-stroke headlines
candidates.angle: 'GLP-1s and your eyes: the good news and the rare risk.' Lead with tirzepatide and retinopathy (observational, 1 year), then put NAION in context. Advise regular eye exams for people with diabetes. Use 'linked to', not 'protects'.
candidates.why_now: Medical Economics resurfaced the story on Oct 3. Eye side effects are trending this week because of the NAION coverage, so a balanced eye-health piece can catch that search spillover.

evidence.signal: Tirzepatide and reduced risk of diabetic retinopathy, multicenter US cohort
Press release, ~174,000 patients from 70 health systems

candidates.topic: 'GLP-1 support' supplement capsules now at Walmart (Lemme): do supplements raise your own GLP-1?
candidates.angle: 'Can a supplement work like Ozempic?' A positive myth-bust: what the evidence says about ingredients sold as GLP-1 boosters, which is far smaller and different from the medicines. Then cover habits with real evidence for supporting your own GLP-1: protein, fibre, eating order. Never imply the supplement replaces a prescription.
candidates.why_now: PR Newswire announced the Walmart launch on Oct 5. Retail Dive and Progressive Grocer are covering the GLP-1 consumer market. Searches for 'natural Ozempic' are high and creators often amplify them uncritically.

evidence.signal: Lemme launches GLP-1 production support capsules at Walmart
GLP-1 users forcing retailers to rethink

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide over 3 years in adults with obesity/overweight and prediabetes: lowest weight points and how much came back (SURMOUNT-1 extension analysis, Obesity Pillars)
candidates.angle: 'Does weight come back on tirzepatide (Zepbound) over time?' Covers what 3-year trial data show about plateaus and small regain while staying on treatment, why a plateau is normal, and the habits that help keep results. Frame it with the exact population and the paper's figures.
candidates.why_now: Newly published in Obesity Pillars (Sep 18). 'Why did my GLP-1 stop working?' is a persistent search, and an earlier snapshot showed a related slow-responder topic at momentum 70.

evidence.signal: Weight nadirs and regain over 3 years of tirzepatide in obesity + prediabetes

candidates.topic: GLP-1 prescriptions for children 8–11 with obesity rose steeply 2019–2026 but remain rare (Pediatrics, 3.5 million children; no GLP-1 approved under 12)
candidates.angle: For parents: what the Pediatrics data actually show (rare, mostly severe obesity, off-label), what's approved for teens, and what to ask a paediatrician. Neutral, no stigma. Note: it's outside our adult core audience, so make it a single Short at most.
candidates.why_now: News4JAX ran it Oct 5 and CBS42 carried a '31,000%' headline. STAT published an op-ed, and Yahoo reported a study on nutritional deficiencies in kids on GLP-1s. Local news numbers conflict (0.03% to 9.3%, 310-fold), so the Pediatrics abstract must be checked before use.

evidence.signal: Trends in GLP-1RA prescriptions for children 8–11 with obesity, 2019–2026
Rare but rising rapidly
Sharp increase headline Oct 5

candidates.topic: Petrelintide (amylin analogue, Zealand/Roche) Phase 2 ZUPREME-1 in The Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology: the 'gentler' next-gen obesity drug
candidates.angle: 'What is amylin, and why is everyone adding it to GLP-1?' An explainer tying together petrelintide, CagriSema and EloraTZP. Report petrelintide's placebo-controlled numbers exactly from the paper (still to be verified). Not approved.
candidates.why_now: Published Sep 29. A Diabetes Therapy review of amylin agonists came out Sep 28, and the Lilly amylin coverage is rising. The amylin theme is building across several sources.

evidence.signal: ZUPREME 1 phase 2 RCT
New amylin-based agonists review

candidates.topic: Semaglutide (Wegovy) and fatty liver: liver fat fell to the normal range in 23 of 26 adults with obesity (small post hoc analysis)
candidates.angle: 'Can Wegovy (semaglutide) clear fatty liver?' Pair the small post hoc result, clearly labelled, with the stronger ESSENCE MASH trial evidence, with population and comparator stated.
candidates.why_now: Medical Daily ran it on Oct 3. Fatty liver is a strong benefits-beyond-weight pillar, and this gives it a fresh hook. The figures still need checking against the source.

evidence.signal: Liver fat to normal in 23 of 26 adults, post hoc

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and skin: Taltz + Zepbound combo data in psoriasis with obesity, plus new reviews on GLP-1s in psoriasis and hidradenitis suppurativa
candidates.angle: 'Can tirzepatide (Zepbound) help psoriasis?' An emerging-research explainer: the combo-trial data Lilly presented, the cohort signals for hidradenitis suppurativa, and what's not yet proven.
candidates.why_now: Lilly announced 21 dermatology presentations at Fall Clinical 2026 (Oct 5), Pluang covered the Taltz-Zepbound data, and Clin Dermatol and JEADV papers came out Oct 1–3.

evidence.signal: 21 dermatology presentations at Fall Clinical 2026
GLP-1RAs in hidradenitis suppurativa, nationwide cohort

candidates.topic: Safiglipron, another oral GLP-1 pill: Phase 3 vs dapagliflozin and placebo-controlled trial in early type 2 diabetes (Nature / Nature Medicine)
candidates.angle: 'How many GLP-1 pills are coming?' A roundup: the Wegovy pill (approved Dec 2025), Foundayo (orforglipron), and safiglipron's new Phase 3 data vs dapagliflozin. Date-hedge every status as of Oct 2026.
candidates.why_now: Nature published the phase 3 trial on Oct 5 and Nature Medicine the placebo-controlled trial on Sep 29. Pills keep drawing search interest ('when will Wegovy pills be available').

evidence.signal: Safiglipron vs dapagliflozin phase 3
Safiglipron in early T2D, placebo-controlled
